column1: # The canonical bytes of P5-1: one line per vector. Source engine = a vector of cic-primitive-engine conformance/canonicalize, checked against the pinned commit
# (testdata/p5/engine-pin.txt) by tools/p5/engine_vectors.py; source own = a vector of this library, checked against a reference written apart in that tool.
# out_of_range = the engine vector holds a float or an integer beyond 64 bits, which this library's value cannot (docs/P5-RESOLVE-MATERIALIZE-RECEIPT.md, decision G).
# Read by rust/tests/canonical_corpus.rs and go/canonical_corpus_test.go. Columns: source, name, status, input, canonical, digest, why (text as JSON string literals).

column7: A4: \\t gets the short escape; \\u0007 (bell) and \\u000B (vertical tab) get the six-character \\u00XX form, lowercase hex.
A7's digest is sha256 of the canonical bytes directly, verified here against Python's hashlib, not against this engine's own digest() in a circle.
A4: Go's json.Marshal escapes <, > and & even though RFC 8259 does not require it; adopted as-is.
A4: U+2028/U+2029 are escaped even though RFC 8259 does not require it -- inherited from Go's json.Marshal.
